Denominators are explicit: 'Attempted' = rows whose outcome is not blank and not 'Not attempted'. Application-blocked attempts stay in 'Attempted' but never count as completed.
Completion rate follows the report: unaided completions / participants who attempted (PDF §9.3). Assisted completion and abandonment are reported separately.
Mean time = mean seconds of COMPLETED attempts only, shown for unaided and for all completions. Abandoned and blocked attempts are excluded from time.
SUS = Brooke scoring on the SUS sheet. With fewer than 10 participants treat the mean as indicative; the reference point ~68 is a commonly cited average.
Pale yellow, blue text = you type here
Grey-blue, black text = formula, do not type here

values: “Responded” does not map directly to the accepted, contacted, waiting and declined counters, causing inconsistent interpretations.
Proxy task traces P01, P02, P03
Required assistance or produced an ambiguous answer.
Label the task and request summary consistently, or add a clearly named response total.
Setting an exact “until 6 pm” availability time is less discoverable than the relative availability options.
One abandonment and four assisted completions.
Add an “Until 6 pm today” shortcut and simplify the exact-time flow.
The relationship detail expected by the scenario is optional and hidden in an expandable section.
Caused hesitation and one assisted completion.
Keep optional details grouped but make their availability clearer in the request flow.
History is not available as a tab, leading first-time users to search the tab bar before finding a secondary path.
Proxy task traces P01, P03, P04
Expose History more prominently or add it to a primary navigation surface.
Denominator for 'Frequency'. Linked to the participant count in Summary.
Disagreement among evaluators; no effect on any participant.
Noticed by participants but caused no error, delay or comment about difficulty.
Caused hesitation, a wrong tap or a recovery without help; low priority to fix.
Needed assistance, or many participants made errors; important to fix before release.
Prevented task completion for one or more participants; must be fixed.
Rate by combining three factors (Nielsen): how often it happens, how big the impact is when it happens, and whether people can get past it once they know.
Frequency alone never sets severity: one participant who could not finish a task is still level 4 for that participant; say so in the description.
Candidate rows (ID CAND-nn) come from reading the code, not from watching people. They stay 'Needs verification' with no severity until observed.
With n = 5 to 8, report counts (e.g. 3/6) rather than percentages, and state the small-sample caveat (PDF §9.3).
